get.summary: A public document the provider fetches, such as client metadata

post.summary: Sign in with email and password
Sign out of the current session
Set a new password with a one-time link

post.description: Sets a new password after checking the current one. Every other session of the user is signed out; this one stays and counts as just re-authenticated. Accounts with two-factor sign-in are refused (422 `two_factor_unavailable`) until a second-factor check exists. A wrong current password is 422 and counts towards the same five-failure lockout as re-authentication; the fifth revokes this session (401).
Refreshes the session's re-authentication time, which approving needs within the last 12 h. The session token stays the same. Five wrong passwords since the last confirmation revoke the session.
post.summary: Confirm the password for the current session

get.summary: The signed-in user and their workspaces

patch.description: Changes the signed-in user's own display name and the language their emails use. Send at least one field. The name is trimmed; null or an empty string clears it.

get.summary: Finish connecting a channel after the provider redirects back

get.description: The workspace policy (null when there is none), the brand overrides, and the policy that applies to a post without a brand. With no workspace policy the strictest default applies: approval required, no self-approval, tolerance 0.

put.description: Owners and admins only. Existing approval requests and destinations keep what they were bound to: a stricter policy applies when a destination is claimed, a looser one never approves anything by itself. A stale expectedVersion is 409.

delete.description: The brand's posts fall back to the workspace policy. Owners and admins only; 404 when the brand has no override.
delete.summary: Remove a brand's approval policy override

put.description: Owners and admins only. Existing approval requests and destinations keep what they were bound to: a stricter policy applies when a destination is claimed, a looser one never approves anything by itself. A stale expectedVersion is 409. 404 when the brand is not in the workspace.
put.summary: Set a brand's approval policy override

post.description: Records the caller's decision on an open request. Approve closes it as approved once the qualifying approvals reach the greater of the request's and the live policy's count; reject and request_changes close it as rejected.
The requester closes their own open request as withdrawn; the post goes back to an editable draft.

post.summary: Start connecting a channel through the provider

get.summary: List the providers this server can connect

post.description: The channel stops publishing; due posts to it are blocked. Its credentials are purged after 30 days. Connecting the same account again restores it. Owners and admins only.
Accepts JPEG, PNG or WebP up to 8 MiB; metadata is stripped before storage.

get.description: The unconfirmed, failed, blocked and awaiting-manual destinations of the posts the caller can see, newest first (limit 1–200, default 100).

The caller's own email preferences in this workspace, per group: failures (failed, unconfirmed and awaiting-manual destinations), approvals (approval requests and decisions) and channels (reconnect and expiry warnings). true means emailed; the default is true for every group. In-app notifications are always shown.

put.description: Replaces the caller's own email preferences in this workspace; every group is required. A group set to false is no longer emailed, but its notifications still appear in-app. Returns the new preferences.

get.description: The caller's own notifications in this workspace, newest first (limit 1–100, default 50); unread=true returns unread ones only. A scoped caller gets only notifications for channels in scope. unread is the caller's total unread count.

post.description: Marks the caller's own notifications read: the listed ids (1–100), or with upTo every unread one up to and including that id (ids order to the millisecond). Ids that aren't the caller's are ignored. Returns the new unread count.

get.description: Either the posts with a destination scheduled in [from, to) (ISO instants, at most 42 days apart; at most 500 posts), or with unscheduled=true the posts with no scheduled destination, newest first (limit 1–100, default 50).

patch.description: Each field given replaces that part whole; variants and destinations replace together. Every destination must be a draft or canceled.

get.description: The 20 newest approval requests of the post, newest first, with what each bound per destination and its decisions.

post.description: Freezes every draft destination for review and opens an approval request; the destinations stay drafts. With a schedule, the approval binds that local time within the policy tolerance.
Cancels every destination that has not published; one that is publishing stops after its current step.
Cancels a failed, blocked or awaiting-manual destination. An unconfirmed one may already be live, so it is refused: mark it published or send it again.
Records that an unconfirmed or awaiting-manual destination is live, as a manual resolution. Its items stay as they are.

Freezes and schedules a failed, blocked or unconfirmed destination again; parts already confirmed live are not sent twice. An unconfirmed one, or one with a part whose send was never confirmed, may already be live, so it needs acknowledgeDuplicate.
Unschedules and schedules again at a local time in a time zone, in one step. Every scheduled destination moves; a post with a destination publishing, verifying or waiting to retry is refused.
Freezes every draft destination and schedules it, at a local time in a time zone or as soon as possible.
Every scheduled or retrying destination goes back to an editable draft.
